doc_title: Public Health Advisory: Ebola Virus Disease Prevention and Response
publisher: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
text:
1. General Situation and Case Notification
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) continues to maintain heightened national surveillance across all points of entry and health facilities. Following confirmed reports of viral hemorrhagic fever activity within the West African sub-region and the confirmation of an imported index case managed in designated isolation facilities, members of the public are advised to remain calm, vigilant, and adhere strictly to preventive measures.

doc_title: Public Health Advisory: Ebola Virus Disease Prevention and Response
publisher: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
text:
2. Symptoms of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD)
Ebola Virus Disease is a severe, often fatal illness in humans. The incubation period—the time interval from infection with the virus to onset of symptoms—is typically between 2 and 21 days. Humans are not infectious until they develop symptoms.

Initial symptoms are sudden and include:
- High fever (temperature equal to or exceeding 37.5°C)
- Severe headache and muscle or joint aches
- Extreme weakness and lethargy
- Sore throat and difficulty swallowing

As the disease progresses, individuals may experience:
- Severe vomiting and persistent diarrhoea
- Abdominal stomach pains
- Impaired kidney and liver function
- In severe stages: unexplained internal and external bleeding, such as bleeding from the gums, nose, eyes, or blood in stool or vomit.

doc_title: Public Health Advisory: Ebola Virus Disease Prevention and Response
publisher: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
text:
3. How the Virus Spreads (Transmission)
Ebola does not spread through airborne transmission (it is not spread through air like influenza or tuberculosis). Transmission occurs through:
- Direct contact (via broken skin or mucous membranes in the eyes, nose, or mouth) with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids (such as saliva, sweat, vomit, urine, or semen) of an infected person.
- Contact with surfaces, clothing, bedding, or medical equipment contaminated with infected fluids.
- Direct contact with the body of a deceased person who died from Ebola. Traditional funeral rituals that involve touching the body must be strictly avoided.
- Direct contact with the blood, meat, or body fluids of infected wild animals, particularly fruit bats, monkeys, and chimpanzees.

doc_title: Public Health Advisory: Ebola Virus Disease Prevention and Response
publisher: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
text:
4. Preventive Guidelines for the Public
The NCDC urges all Nigerians and residents to practice the following:
- Hand Hygiene: Wash hands frequently and thoroughly with clean running water and soap, or use an alcohol-based hand rub with at least 60% alcohol.
- Physical Distancing: Avoid physical contact with anyone who presents with unexplained fever and bleeding.
- Food Safety: Avoid hunting, handling, or consuming wild bushmeat. Ensure all animal products are cooked thoroughly before consumption.
- Suspected Exposure: If you suspect that you or someone near you has had contact with an infected person or exhibits symptoms, isolate immediately in a separate room and alert health authorities. Do not attempt self-medication.

To report suspected cases, seek verified guidance, or request medical dispatch, contact the NCDC immediately through official verified channels:

doc_title: Consumer Protection Advisory: Digital Money Lending Applications and Defamatory Debt Recovery Practices
publisher: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
section_title: 1. Regulatory Status of Digital Money Lenders (DMLs)
text:
1. Regulatory Status of Digital Money Lenders (DMLs)
The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), in conjunction with the Joint Regulatory and Enforcement Task Force (JRETF), reminds members of the public that only Digital Money Lenders (DMLs) registered under the Limited Interim Regulatory Framework are authorized to offer online credit services in Nigeria. Unregistered lending applications operating through direct APK distribution, third-party social media download links, or unverified app marketplaces are strictly illegal.

doc_title: Consumer Protection Advisory: Digital Money Lending Applications and Defamatory Debt Recovery Practices
publisher: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
section_title: 2. Prohibited Debt Recovery Methods and Harassment
text:
2. Prohibited Debt Recovery Methods and Harassment
Under Sections 17 and 18 of the FCCPA (2018), digital lenders are strictly prohibited from engaging in abusive, coercive, or defamatory recovery practices. Specifically:
- Accessing or scraping borrower contact lists, personal photos, or storage without explicit, verifiable consent is unlawful.
- Sending mass defamation text messages, funeral posters, or threatening messages to contacts, employers, or relatives of borrowers is illegal and constitutes criminal cyber-harassment.
- Unilateral imposition of interest rates exceeding approved ceilings or arbitrary processing penalties is illegal.
- Licensed financial institutions and authorized DMLs will never threaten physical harm or publish personal data on public online forums.

doc_title: Consumer Protection Advisory: Digital Money Lending Applications and Defamatory Debt Recovery Practices
publisher: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
section_title: 3. Red Flags of Fake and Fraudulent Loan Applications
text:
3. Red Flags of Fake and Fraudulent Loan Applications
Consumers should remain vigilant against predatory loan operators exhibiting the following characteristics:
- Requiring upfront registration fees, administrative deposits, or processing clearing fees before loans are disbursed.
- Distributing application installation files (.apk) directly via WhatsApp, Telegram, or unsolicited SMS messages rather than recognized platforms.
- Demanding access to device contacts, media libraries, and call logs as an mandatory prerequisite for microloans.
- Falsely claiming partnership with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) or Federal Government welfare schemes.

text:
4. How to Verify Approved Lenders and File Complaints
Consumers who experience harassment, defamation, or unauthorized account deductions from digital lenders are urged to report immediately:
- Check the official whitelist of approved and conditionally approved digital lenders at: https://fccpc.gov.ng/approved-dmls
- Official FCCPC Consumer Protection Hotline: 0800 033 2272 (Toll-Free, Monday – Friday 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM)
- Dedicated DML Harassment Reporting Desk: dmlcompliance@fccpc.gov.ng
- Official Online Complaint Form: https://fccpc.gov.ng/complaints

doc_title: National Social Safety Nets Project: Guidelines for Conditional Cash Transfer Verification and Anti-Fraud Safeguards
publisher: National Social Safety Nets Project (NASSP) / Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs
section_title: 1. Official National Social Register (NSR) Enrollment Procedure
text:
1. Official National Social Register (NSR) Enrollment Procedure
The National Social Safety Nets Project (NASSP) and the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs maintain the verified National Social Register (NSR) of poor and vulnerable households. 
- Enrollment in the National Social Register is strictly community-based and conducted in person through trained local government enumerators using official electronic data capture devices.
- Citizens cannot be registered into the social register via unsolicited social media links, text messages, or third-party web portals.
- All beneficiary identities are validated using the National Identity Number (NIN) and Bank Verification Number (BVN) to ensure direct, verifiable disbursement.

doc_title: National Social Safety Nets Project: Guidelines for Conditional Cash Transfer Verification and Anti-Fraud Safeguards
publisher: National Social Safety Nets Project (NASSP) / Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs
section_title: 2. Safeguards Against Fake Grant Schemes and Fraud
text:
2. Safeguards Against Fake Grant Schemes and Fraud
Members of the public are cautioned against widespread fraudulent messages circulating on WhatsApp, Facebook, and SMS claiming to offer federal grants or cash transfers:
- The Federal Government never charges any application fee, registration fee, card issuance fee, or validation payment to receive social assistance or palliative transfers. Any portal requesting money to release funds is fraudulent.
- Official disbursements are transferred directly into verified personal bank accounts or authorized mobile money wallets linked to the beneficiary's NIN. Cash handovers by political intermediaries are prohibited.
- The government does not require beneficiaries to share card PINs, CVV codes, or one-time passwords (OTPs) under any circumstance.

doc_title: Regulations and Guidelines for Voting Procedures and BVAS Accreditation
text:
1. Mandatory Accreditation Through BVAS
In accordance with the Electoral Act, accreditation of voters using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) is mandatory for every election conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).
- A voter must physically present an authentic Permanent Voter Card (PVC) issued by INEC at the specific polling unit where they are registered.
- Accreditation is confirmed solely by matching fingerprint biometric data or facial recognition on the BVAS device against the registered voter database.
- Manual accreditation, incident forms, and voting by proxy are strictly abolished and illegal under current electoral guidelines. If BVAS cannot authenticate a voter either through fingerprint or facial recognition, that voter cannot vote.

doc_title: Regulations and Guidelines for Voting Procedures and BVAS Accreditation
text:
2. Polling Unit Operations and Timelines
- Official voting hours at all polling units nationwide commence at 8:30 AM and conclude at 2:30 PM.
- Every eligible voter already standing in line at or before 2:30 PM must be accredited and allowed to cast their ballot. Polling unit officials may not close queues prematurely.
- Accreditation and voting take place simultaneously.
- Voting is entirely free. No election official or community representative may demand payments or administrative dues from voters.

doc_title: Regulations and Guidelines for Voting Procedures and BVAS Accreditation
section_title: 3. Neutrality and Official INEC Information Channels
text:
3. Neutrality and Official INEC Information Channels
INEC maintains strict political neutrality. Unofficial online claims alleging cancellation of voting, sudden polling unit relocation, or online electronic ballot submission via third-party web apps are false. All verified operational announcements are transmitted only via:
- INEC Citizens' Contact Centre (ICCC) Toll-Free Hotline: 0700-CALL-INEC (0700 2255 4632)
- Secondary Helplines: 0818 095 8615, 0818 095 8616
- Official Verification Portal: https://inecnigeria.org
- Official WhatsApp Verification Channel: +234 816 096 8218
